name: Eyes of the Shaman
body:
School divination; Level cleric/oracle 2, occultist 2, shaman 2, sorcerer/wizard 2, witch 2

Casting Time 1 round

Components V, S, DF

Effect cone-shaped emanation

Duration concentration, up to 1 minute/level (D)

Saving Throw none (see text); Spell Resistance no

This spell functions as detect demon and detect evil, except as above and it detects only the auras of spirits (fey, outsiders, and incorporeal undead) in many forms. This includes their presence when possessing a creature or object, the direct effects of their on-going magic (spells or spell-like), and any lingering spiritual auras shed by spirits. If a spirit has an ability or feat that would allow them a chance to avoid detection, they can still do so against this spell. The amount of information revealed depends on how long you study a particular area or subject.

1st Round: Presence or absence of spirit auras. Spirit auras may also be detected on creatures who are otherwise tainted by spirits. Creatures tainted by spirits includes those who have a bloodline or heritage from a spirit (such as a sorcerer’s fey bloodline), are affected by a spirit’s abilities (such as a fey’s token, a demon’s profane gift, or otherwise imbued with a spirit’s essence), grafted or implanted with part of a spirit’s essence or form, possess an Obedience feat related to a spirit ruler (see below), or under significant spiritual influence as determined by the GM. Additionally, this spell detects whether or not a portal or similar magical passage leads to an Inner or Outer plane.
2nd Round: Number of spirit auras in the area and the strength of the strongest spirit aura present. If you are of good alignment and the strongest spirit aura’s strength is overwhelming, and the HD or level of the spirit aura’s source is at least twice your character level, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends.
3rd Round: The power and location of each spirit aura, and what spirit ruler, if any, a detected spirit is most closely affiliated with. If a spirit aura is outside your line of sight, then you discern its direction but not its exact location. This spell may reveal a spirit’s affiliation to a spirit ruler (such as a fey ruler, outsider lord, etc.) but such spirits receive a Will saving throw to resist you learning this information. If a spirit succeeds at this saving throw or is not forsworn to a spirit ruler, you know only that this aspect of the spell returns no information.

Aura Power: The strength of a spirit aura is determined by the HD of the spirit or the caster level of the source, as given on the table below.

Lingering Spirit Aura: A spirit aura lingers after its original source dissipates (in the case of a spell or ability) or is destroyed (in the case of a creature or magic item). If cast and directed at such a location, this spell indicates an aura strength of dim (even weaker than a faint aura). How long the aura lingers at this dim level depends on its original power, as shown below.
